item.title: Rock on the Rise, Pop Drops: Five-Year Trends on Billboard’s Radio Songs Chart
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest trends in music. Today, we're looking at the Billboard Radio Songs chart over the past five years. What's been making waves on the airwaves? Let's find out.
[Music transitions]
Host: According to ChartCipher's latest research, rock music is on the rise, growing from 10% to 24% of the chart between 2021 and 2025. That's more than doubling its footprint. Examples of rock hits that made it big include sombr's "Back to Friends", Hozier's "Too Sweet", and Glass Animals' "Heat Waves".
[Short music clip plays]
Host: On the other hand, pop music has been on the decline, falling from 52% to 35% over the same period. Country music has remained steady, with a slight dip from 31% to 29%. The top five genres on the Radio Songs chart in 2025 are pop, country, rock, hip-hop/rap, and dance/club/electronic.
[Music transitions]
Host: Now, let's talk about the instruments that are dominating the airwaves. It turns out that drums and bass are almost universal, with nearly 93% to 96% of hits featuring these instruments. Guitar use has also increased, from 60% to 68%, as rock music gains popularity. However, piano use has taken a hit, dropping from 35% to just 11% over the five-year period.
[Short music clip plays]
Host: Finally, what about the lyrics? It seems that cynical and detached are the most prevalent moods, with increases of 29 and 19 percentage points, respectively. Anger is also on the rise, with a 16 percentage point increase. But don't worry, there's some positive news too - happy and optimistic lyrics have also been on the rise, with 38% and 37% of hits featuring these moods in 2025.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's a wrap on our look at the Billboard Radio Songs chart over the past five years. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode.
[Outro music continues to play]
